I would recommend you get a proper receiver. You say you have an "amp" and you could mean "receiver" but I'm not sure. A receiver does a bunch of things. First, it allows you to have multiple inputs and one output. So your HTPC and mp3 jukebox are wired into the receiver and then the output lines of the receiver go to the speakers. The receiver also decodes signals such as Dolby Digital, DTS, &c. So once you have this setup, you switch the input on the receiver to change what shows up on screen or comes out of the speakers. More advanced receivers have networking options that allow you to connect to a streaming server. I would advise that their interfaces are not great at all so it's not an important factor.

Freeview is the name for the UK wide digital TV broadcast of about 800 channels and radio stations.

I will chime in on the OS side of the house, since that is what I have been rampaging about for a while.

I've personally been enjoying Manjaro, which is an Arch derivative. This is for two main reasons; the first being it is updated weekly so far, pushing security updates and moving towards general system stability, with the second being that it has access to the AUR, which can be daunting, but worthwhile, I think. I would recommend against Manjaro if you want to be given full control of everything in your system without wrangling it away. The installer is wanting, but improving as of the latest news article. Manjaro also comes with Steam preloaded(a bold move for a system trying to eliminate as much non-free software as possible).

Debian is a good suggestion as well, since SteamOS is being released as a derivative of it. It may be possible to only install SteamOS and then install packages as needed to make it a media center as you see fit. At that point you could install Kodi as well and have a full screen gaming center and a media center.

The largest benefit that linux offers over other systems is the very wide variety of distrobutions and the communities supporting those distrobutions for themselves. By joining any of those communities you have the opportunity for recieving help and helping others as your knowledge increases with time.
